title: IFS Food version 8 – the system in practice
subtitle: Scoring · KO requirements · HACCP · operational processes · measurement and improvement · audit
note: Original QA Support material. It does not replace the official text of the standard, the certification protocol or IFS-licensed training. Before an audit, use current IFS documents.
footer: TR-002 · IFS Food v8 · QA Support

slides.title: Learning objectives
bullets: Explain what IFS Food is and how certification works
Know the structure of version 8 and the 10 KO requirements
Understand scoring and certification levels
Identify evidence of implementation for key requirements
Prepare an action plan after the audit
Compare IFS and BRCGS

slides.title: IFS Food in brief
bullets: Standard for manufacturers and packers of loose food, GFSI-benchmarked
Widespread among retail suppliers in Germany, France, Italy, Poland
Version 8: published April 2023, mandatory since 1 January 2024
234 requirements in 5 chapters
Food defence moved into chapter 4 (4.21)

slides.title: Version 8 structure
table: customer, specifications, purchasing, cleaning, foreign material, traceability, allergens, food fraud, food defence
audits, calibration, testing, complaints, recalls, CAPA

slides.title: Requirement scoring
slides.callout: Major: −15% · KO scored D: −50% and no certificate · KO only A, B or D

slides.title: 10 KO requirements
table: specifications of raw materials, packaging, rework

slides.title: Result and levels
table: no KO at D and no major, score ≥ 95%
no KO at D and no major, score 75–95%

slides.title: Exercise 1 – calculate the score
bullets: 200 requirements: 180 × A, 15 × B, 4 × C, 1 × D (not KO)
Possible: 200 × 20 = 4000 points
Achieved: 3600 + 225 + 20 − 20 = 3825 points
Score: 95.6% → Higher Level
Your task: what happens if 2 A scores become D?

slides.title: Chapters 1–2 – evidence
table: legible, protected, kept ≥ shelf life + 1 year
limit validation, KO 2 – CCP records, verification ≥ 1×/year

slides.title: Chapter 3
bullets: Hygiene rules based on risk assessment
KO 3: rules applied by staff, contractors and visitors – observed on the floor
Protective clothing: cleanliness, changing, laundering
Illness reporting procedure
Training in an understood language, effectiveness assessment
Staff facilities and hygiene locks

slides.title: Customer and specifications (KO 4, KO 5)
bullets: Procedure for establishing and communicating customer requirements
Compliance with agreements: recipe, process, testing, packaging, label
Specifications for all raw materials, packaging and rework
Product specifications compliant with law and agreements
slides.callout: Most common risk: mismatch between recipe, label and customer specification

slides.title: Key chapter 4 requirements
table: raw material risk assessment, suppliers, services

slides.title: Exercise 2 – customer compliance
bullets: Choose a product for a key customer
Compare: customer specification, recipe, label, testing plan
Record every discrepancy
Each discrepancy = risk of a D score on KO 4

slides.title: Chapter 5
table: programme for all requirements, critical areas ≥ 1×/year

slides.title: Audit process
table: corrections, root causes, actions and deadlines – usually within 2 weeks of the preliminary report

slides.title: Writing the action plan
bullets: Correction: what was done immediately
Root cause: with evidence of analysis
Corrective action: what changes permanently
Responsible person and deadline
How effectiveness will be verified
slides.callout: 'Employee retrained' is rarely a sufficient action

slides.title: IFS vs. BRCGS
table: number and class of non-conformities, AA–D

slides.title: Summary
bullets: IFS scores every requirement – every detail counts
10 KO requirements = priority for implementation and internal audits
Compliance with customer agreements is the foundation of IFS
The action plan needs root cause analysis, not just corrections
Next: final exercise and test (15 questions, pass mark 80%)
